question.problem: The professor of geometry notices that, on average, every batch of practice questions contains $6$ questions that cite the interior angle theorem in the solution. What is the probability that in the next batch of practice questions, there will be more than $5$ questions that cite the interior angle theorem in the solution? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that questions that cite the interior angle theorem in the solution occur independently and at a constant average rate.
question.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of questions that cite the interior angle theorem in the solution. Since the average rate is $6$ questions that cite the interior angle theorem in the solution per batch, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, the number of questions that cite the interior angle theorem in the solution can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda =6,$ and we can write $X∼\text{Po}(6).$ 

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{6}^{x}{e}^{-6}}{x!}
$$

To compute $P(X>5),$ we will use the complement:

$$
P(X>5)=1-P(X\le 5)
$$

Computing the probability of the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 5) & =P(X\in {0,1,2,3,4,5}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4)+f(5) \\  & =\frac{{6}^{0}{e}^{-6}}{0!}+\frac{{6}^{1}{e}^{-6}}{1!}+\frac{{6}^{2}{e}^{-6}}{2!}+\frac{{6}^{3}{e}^{-6}}{3!}+\frac{{6}^{4}{e}^{-6}}{4!}+\frac{{6}^{5}{e}^{-6}}{5!} \\  & ≈0.446\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, the probability of finding more than $5$ questions that cite the interior angle theorem in the solution in the next batch of practice questions is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>5) & =1-P(X\le 5) \\  & ≈1-0.446 \\  & =0.554\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
